title: HHS Decertifies Kentucky Organ Group After Finding Persistent Patient Safety Failures
text:
The Trump administration on Wednesday began stripping federal certification from Network for Hope, the organ procurement organization serving Kentucky and parts of Indiana, Ohio, and West Virginia.

Kentucky Man's Case Highlighted
Kennedy pointed to the case of T.J. Hoover, a Kentucky man who showed signs of awareness on an operating table moments before doctors were set to remove his organs."Physicians refused to proceed with the organ recovery because they believed that he was still alive," Kennedy said at the press conference. "T.J. we are grateful that you're here, and we're grateful to those physicians who had the courage to do the right thing."
Reviews Cited Widespread Problems
A separate HRSA review of 351 cases from 2021 to 2024 found concerning features in 103 of them, including 73 patients showing neurological signs inconsistent with organ donation. The review also raised questions about whether some potential donors were actually deceased when procurement began, and pointed to weak medical evaluations, poor coordination among medical teams, and questionable consent practices.Kennedy said the Biden administration was aware of safety problems at the organization but failed to act. HRSA Administrator Tom Engels said his agency spent the past year working with Network for Hope on corrective steps, but the organization never showed sufficient improvement. CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz said the decision should serve as a warning to other providers that fail to protect patients.
